soundness_flags.label: symbols theta_minus/theta_plus and def:watson-published-reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: The endpoint definitions take sqrt(delta(P)) and declare values in K for every P, although P_W permits delta(P)<0 and the K-restricted sublevel set is only the raw endpoint interval after feasibility and nontruncation are established.

soundness_flags.label: def:retained-bootstrap and thm:contact-endpoint-and-retention-law
soundness_flags.one_line: The retained empirical-bootstrap procedure omits the number of draws and an output convention when no draw is retained, so it does not define a finite-sample random object even though the totalization claim is presented as every-sample.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: def:watson-published-reduction
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The p=2 sharp-set and endpoint reduction is imported from Watson et al. rather than reproved.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All contact and inference claims are conditional on the published p=2 reduction.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:uniform-multiplier-coupling; thm:adaptive-score-hull; upper half of thm:minimax-loss-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Uniform multiplier approximation and uniform integrability are explicitly unresolved by the open-ended question.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Whole-set coverage and the adaptive upper loss rates are claimed only conditional on an affirmative resolution of the multiplier-coupling question.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3693–3695, Corollary 2.1 and §3.3/Theorem 4; p. 3707, Appendix A.9
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Corollary 2.1 gives the scalar p=2 endpoint formula. Theorem 4 samples subject to feasibility tau >= tau-hat_p,(b); Appendix A.9 asserts smoothness and asymptotic validity while conditioning on feasible resamples.

source_verification_receipts.locator: bibliographic landing page, pp. 399–405; primary full text inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Verified the cited boundary-bootstrap paper and publication details; no theorem-text mismatch is asserted.
The paper characterizes standard-bootstrap consistency for directionally differentiable maps with Gaussian first-stage limits and states failure when the resulting limit is non-Gaussian.
The paper constructs random sets covering an identified set and gives conditions for uniform asymptotic validity over P.
The paper obtains uniformly valid critical values through a bootstrap approximation to a subset of the local parameter space and uses Gaussian multipliers.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible author preprint states Gaussian and conditional Gaussian-multiplier approximation for maxima of sums of high-dimensional random vectors; no primary-version formula comparison is asserted.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract, pp. 1769–1790; full theorem text inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The official abstract states impossibility of locally asymptotically unbiased and alpha-quantile-unbiased estimation for nondifferentiable targets.
The paper studies a numerical bootstrap under fixed and drifting sequences, including constrained/nonstandard estimators and partially identified test statistics.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference 236, Article 106245, 2025
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives uniformly valid inference for root-n constrained-optimization estimators at or drifting toward a boundary; it is framed around point estimators rather than partially identified sets.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make raw endpoints partial objects defined only for delta(P)>=0, state Theta_I(P)=K intersect [theta_-(P),theta_+(P)], and prove the parameter-margin condition removes K truncation on the relevant classes.

Specify the retained-bootstrap finite-sample experiment completely: number of resamples, whether it is rejection sampling or a fixed-B retained empirical law, and the output when no draw is feasible; then restate the kernel theorem for that exact object.

Resolve the coupling OEQ as a finite-dimensional multiplier theorem with an explicit uniform-integrability bound, converting the conditional hull and matching upper frontier into unconditional results.

Add a direct comparison with Hong--Li numerical bootstrap and Li's proximal bootstrap that explains why their corrected schemes do not deliver a whole identified-set hull or the fourth-root endpoint target.

recommended_next_step: Continue revision on this angle: repair the two undefined finite-sample/domain objects, then advance the explicitly conditional multiplier result only after its uniform coupling route is sharpened.
